newsitem.title: CANADA: Bombardier posts record fourth-quarter profits.
newsitem.headline: Bombardier posts record fourth-quarter profits.

text.p: Fourth-quarter profits at Bombardier Inc soared to their highest quarterly level ever, the Montreal-based aerospace and transportation equipment maker said on Wednesday.

Bombardier earned C$147.3 million ($109 million) or C$0.42 ($0.31) a share in its latest quarter ended Jan. 31, compared with a loss of C$49.9 million ($37 million) or C$0.15 ($0.11) a share in the 1995 quarter, which included a writedown of C$155 million $114.7 million) or C$0.44 ($0.33) a share on its investment in share units of Eurotunnel.
Revenues were C$2.5 billion ($1.85 billion) versus C$2.7 billion ($2 billion).

For the full year, Bombardier earned C$406.2 million ($300.5 million) or C$1.16 ($0.86) a share in 1996, compared with C$158 million ($117 million) or C$0.45 ($0.33) a share after the Eurotunnel investment writedown.
Annual revenues were C$8 billion ($6 billion) in 1996, versus C$7.1 billion ($5.2 billion) in 1995.

Bombardier received the Eurotunnel shares in 1994 as settlement for the supply of shuttle-train cars for the English Channel tunnel. In fiscal 1996, Bombardier wrote down the value of its holding of Eurotunnel shares to reflect their actual market value at the time.

Analysts said Bombardier's quarterly earnings came in on target, driven mainly by strong sales in its aircraft and motororized consumer products divisions and a solid performance by the company's financial services unit, which provides inventory financing mainly for other companies.
"Profits were right in line with expectations, very strong," said an analyst who declined to be identified.

Commenting on year profits, Laurent Beaudoin, chairman and chief executive officer, said sales grew in all of the company's business segments, but difficulties at the Belgium-based BN Division of Bombardier Eurorail prevented the company's transportation sector from reaching its expected level of profitability.
Bombardier Class B common shares shares fell C$0.55 to C$26.05 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday after the fourth-quarter results were released.
Analysts said they were not troubled by the share price drop.
"The stock has had such a strong run, it always does this. It takes a breather, and a week later there is a new (aircraft or railcar) order and everybody comes back in," the analyst said.

Bombardier makes turboprop and jet aircraft, including business jets, at its facilities in Canada, the United States and Ireland. Its transportation equipment group includes urban transit and rail transportation equipment operations in Europe and North America. Its motorized consumer products include snowmobiles and boats.
